data.name: RACE: Caterham Expansion
data.detailed_description:
Celebrating the 50-year anniversary of Caterham Cars Ltd, RACE fans can now expand the WTCC Experience with this exceptional series of classic sportscars. RACE: CATERHAM introduces a total of 60 individual new cars/car skins based on some of the most exciting models in the Caterham sports car range, including the Caterham CSR 200, CSR 260 and the CSR 320 Concept, a concept version with a grueling 320hp.
Racers can run the cars on two exciting new tracks: the legendary Imola circuit and the former GP track Estoril.
RACE: CATERHAM includes new features that improve the original RACE game experience: improved performance scalability, a performance monitor to help the player find the best possible graphical settings, and a new controller interface with more options for joy-pad or keyboard/mouse controls.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimo:
  • Microsoft Windows XP Home/Pro
  • Processador Intel Pentium 4 a 1,7 GHz ou 100% compatível
  • 512 MB de RAM
  • 2,5 GB de espaço livre em disco
  • Placa gráfica compatível com DirectX 9, com 128 MB de memória
  • Placa de som compatível com DirectX 9
  • Teclado e rato
  • DirectX versão 9
Recomendado:
  • Microsoft Windows XP Home/Pro
  • Processador Intel Pentium IV a 3 GHz ou 100% compatível
  • 1 GB de RAM
  • 2,5 GB de espaço livre em disco
  • Placa gráfica compatível com DirectX 9, com 256 MB de memória
  • Placa de som compatível com DirectX 9
  • Volante com "force feedback", compatível com DirectX 9
  • DirectX versão 9
Graphic Cards not supported:
  • NVIDIA GeForce 3/4 cards
  • ATI Radeon 8500/9000/9200
  • Intel Motherboard mounted chipsets

reviews.review:
Tags: Driving & Racing - Simbin
Additional Tags: Delete Local Content & Remove from Library

TLDR: Play RaceRoom instead. SimBin whom made the Race07/WTCC/GT titles offers a variety of older racing games. Standout features are varied. Too dated.

In theory one can make one of the most realistic steering wheel racing experiences using some of the IP Simbin has on offer. I think I remember saying they had attached a variety of sensors on real life cars and translated the data into the engine with impressive results. 

Being able to mod extensively seems an interesting avenue to streamline the content from all the products, improve the UI, add more tracks... I would start slow and proceed methodically, starting by hunting down discussion groups online or a fan site. 

Setting up a steering wheel is a dedicated passion project that requires quite a fair bit of logistics, it is a bit like VR, where you preferrably have to dedicate a space of your house for it. It is not for everyone. I am glad to own a copy of this series as it does seem to have quite a bit of quality features but the lack of accessibility, age and somewhat obscure qualities makes it best kept in the archive rather than on central display in your permanent library. As such I will remove it to hidden library for declutter along with the rest of the SimBin collection. 

Conclusion: There is no shortage of quality racing games using modern engines to pick from, and some have decent handling and physics of their own. Unless you go all out with the simulation project and mod this IP in and out and bust the steering wheel out it is unlikely to really compete or compare all that well in a simple KB+M, regular user type of experience. If i ever get serious enough I'll just go dig back for this game in the archive or get a newer franchise that accomplishes the same thing such as Raceroom
